Deputy "default" finished job 01a1956e-109e-7ac1-8537-74c0feeb701b: rc 0 (ok).
Command: aida add --type story --priority high --parent EPIC-612 --tags vendor:codex,mail-wake --title Codex mail wake works for every Codex seat, not only aida agent new launches; doctor flags an uninstalled wake service --description ## Why
Codex mail wake is built (STORY-2136, TASK-2347, TASK-2532), but tonight nothing is armed and `aida mailbox wake-service status` reports `installed: false`. Arming happens only through `aida agent new codex`. A Codex seat started any other way never gets woken for mail, for example `aida session start --owns ID` then `codex`, the way the operator ran TASK-2631. Mail to a Codex seat then sits until its next turn.

## Acceptance
1. The Codex SessionStart hook arms mail wake for any Codex session in an AIDA project that has a registry row, whatever launched it, using the exact thread id from the hook (never `--last`). `[agents.codex] mail_wake = false` and `--no-mail-wake` still opt out.
2. When the service is not installed, the hook installs it with the existing bounded `systemctl --user` call. If that is refused (e.g. containment), the agent starts anyway and prints the one command to run, and its row reads `failed`, not `pending`.
3. `aida doctor` (default checks, not only `check codex-mail-wake`) reports a finding when any live Codex agent exists and the wake service is not installed, with the fix command.
4. `aida session start --owns ID` on a Codex project prints whether mail wake will arm (ties to BUG-2379's Next: block).
5. End-to-end fixture: a hand-started Codex session gets a row that reads `armed`; mail to its handle produces exactly one queued notification; ending it retires the row.
6. docs/agents/codex-mail-wake.md says hand-launched Codex seats are covered.
